reason: E3 supports that fast synthesis avoids phase segregation, but none of the cited evidence addresses the mechanistic link from SRO to electronic structure to suppressed diffusion. E1 and E2 discuss SRO and diffusion in bulk alloys, not nanoalloys, and do not connect SRO to diffusion suppression via electronic structure.
premises: Rapid synthesis can trap a metastable, well-mixed atomic configuration in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Short-range chemical order (SRO) can be established during synthesis and retained.
SRO tailors local electronic structure and bond environments.
This tailored electronic structure suppresses atomic diffusion at high temperatures.
Suppressed diffusion reduces the thermodynamic drive for phase segregation.
